hyp1.note: the IL-23/IL23R axis drives Crohn disease (mechanism: variants 'increase IL-23/Th17 pathway activity'); the chain starts at IL12B; IL23R appears only in step notes, never as a node

hyp2.note: sign from the mechanism: 'loss-of-function variants in NOD2 and LACC1 ... promote chronic intestinal inflammation'; the chain starts at the proteins, the mechanism names loss-of-function variants

hyp3.note: the chain starts at 'GPR35 risk variants'; the mechanism makes KYNA-GPR35 signalling protective, so the variants act by loss of signalling

findings.detail: The one link from IL-23 signalling to Th17 has polarity 'unknown' though its own note says 'promotes'; its citations are two STRING enrichments and a GWAS abstract that never names Th17, so hyp1 has no signed route.
IL23R, one of hyp1's two genes, is never a node of the chain (it appears only in the notes of hyp1.2 and hyp1.4), so the IL23R claim has no route.
All three citations for 'Th17-mediated inflammation leads to Crohn disease' (PMID:17068223, rs7517847, rs11209026) are IL23R variant-disease associations: they back the step's note, not the step.

The note says 'IL23R variants confer risk', but the cited PMID:17068223 says the coding variant rs11209026 (Arg381Gln) 'confers strong protection', and its GWAS row gives the common G allele (frequency 0.93) as the risk allele; the run never registers a protective IL23R allele.

Subunit membership ('IL12B is a subunit of IL-23') is written as increases_amount; of its citations only IL12B's UniProt entry says so, while the IL23R entry and the IL12B-IL23R STRING edge are about the receptor.
hyp2.2 ends at 'Innate immune response'; hyp2.3 starts at LACC1.
hyp2.3 ends at 'Enhanced cytokine secretion'; hyp2.4 starts at 'Dysregulated bacterial sensing and macrophage function'.

The chain says NOD2 and LACC1 promote detection, innate immunity and cytokine secretion, then jumps to 'dysregulated' function causing Crohn disease, so it never says whether loss or gain causes disease; the mechanism asserts loss of function, while the cited PMID:11385576 proposes 'altering the recognition ... and/or over-activating NF-kB', which includes gain.

PMID:11385576 is the NOD2-Crohn association paper; it says the leucine-rich repeat is a receptor for 'components of microbial pathogens', not peptidoglycan, and the run cites it for detection rather than for the disease association it reports.

The LACC1 UniProt entry the run cites says LACC1 promotes NOD2-induced cytokine secretion but also 'likely' triggers 'polyamine-mediated proinflammatory cytokine suppression'; the run uses only the first.

The disease step cites three GWAS rows (variant-disease associations, two with no allele) and PMID:40089498, which is about T cells, not macrophages or bacterial sensing; nothing cited states dysregulated sensing or macrophage function causing Crohn disease.

'Metabolic-immune crosstalk' is a vague node standing in for concrete ones the cited texts name (KYNA, mesenteric white-to-beige adipose browning, M2 macrophage polarisation, adipose thermogenic and anti-inflammatory gene expression), so expressible claims became inexpressible.

Read literally, 'GPR35 signaling dysregulation' is required_for (+) crosstalk and 'disrupted' crosstalk leads to (+) Crohn disease, so dysregulation would lower disease and the risk variants would be protective; the chain contradicts its own mechanism.

The variant-to-signalling step cites GWAS rows that state only association with Crohn disease (no allele named; rs3749171 from a five-disease pleiotropy analysis) and a UniProt entry that never mentions variants; no text says the variants change GPR35 signalling.

The proposed falsification (a GPR35 agonist should reduce colitis in mice) is what the cited PMID:40623474 already reports: KYNA browned mesenteric fat via GPR35-ERK1/2-PGC-1a and alleviated colitis in IL-10-/- and TNBS mice.

Four chain citations are STRING over-representation results computed on the run's own 7 input genes (GOCC:0072536, GO:0032740, GO:2000330, GO:0045087); they restate the genes' annotations and cannot support a causal step.
The rs2066847 GWAS row gives odds ratio 3.103 with a confidence interval of 1.497-1.618, which does not contain it; the run passes the row on unchecked.

rs1373904 and rs34236350 have risk allele '?' with beta 'increase', and rs5743293 and rs3749171 have no allele and no effect size, so none gives a direction for any allele, yet they are cited as Crohn risk evidence.
contradicting_evidence is empty for all three hypotheses, though the run's own sources include a protective IL23R allele (PMID:17068223) and a cytokine-suppressing LACC1 role (Q8IV20).
Confidence 'high' and support 'grounded', yet no claim composes and the disease step is supported only by variant associations that do not state it.
Confidence 'high' and support 'grounded', yet the chain breaks twice, its disease step has no supporting text, and the loss-of-function direction is never stated in a step.
MEIS1 and TRIM4 are left unexplained; TRIM4 is one of the five genes in the innate-immune-response enrichment the run cites (STRING:GO:0045087) but no hypothesis uses it.

Amount of a protein complex: the IL-23 heterodimer has only a GO component term (GO:0070743), render.py allows amount targets only for protein, chemical or gene, while Lean's Target.amount takes any kind, so 'IL12B raises IL-23' cannot be stated.

The guide's undirected-change rule covers objects ('leads to abnormal X') but not undirected subjects ('dysregulated X leads to D'); I applied the 'abnormal X' phenotype rule to the subject (UPHENO:0085601, species-neutral, not in the guide's prefix table).
The guide maps increases_amount to an amount target only; for a process object ('Enhanced cytokine secretion', GO:0001816) I used a process target.
Statement.distinctEvidence keeps one item per PMID or ref regardless of polarity, so S5's refuting Q8IV20 span is dropped and S5 fuses to b=4/5, d=0 although the record states both directions.
BLN:GPR35-CrohnRiskVariants stands for the run's class 'GPR35 risk variants'; no single ID, and neither cited rsID row names an allele.
